newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market slow at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market slow at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Wednesday was slow, with light "clean-up" activity reported following Tuesday's brisk sales, feedlot sources said.

About 1,000 head sold in Kansas at $72.00 per cwt, steady with Tuesday's top price there, sources said. A few packer bids were reported at $71.00, but generally were passed as cattle owners continued to ask mostly $73.00, they said.
Showlists in Kansas were close to or already sold, with USDA near midday Thursday, reporting 74,200 head sold for the week to date, nearly matching trade showlist estimates.

Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots also were close to being sold out of market ready animals, but still had cattle to offer. However, a large percentage of those cattle had 100 days or less, on feed, sources said.
USDA Tuesday reported 43,700 head sold in the Panhandle which brought the week-to-date figure to 53,400. Trade estimates for this week's showlist were close to 72,000 head.
Cattle prices were supported by strong beef demand at higher prices and tight supplies of choice graded beef.
